APM a93J02: ∑(−1)n/(n+1)=log⁡2 via dominated convergence

1. Informal proof

Why it’s hard. The geometric series 1/(1+x)=∑(−x)n converges only for |x|<1, yet we need to integrate up to x=1 (where the series converges conditionally but not absolutely). Interchanging the sum and integral requires justification beyond termwise integration of a uniformly convergent series, since the convergence is not uniform on [0,1].

The key insight. Integrate the partial sums Sn⁢(x)=∑k=0n(−x)k=(1−(−x)n+1)/(1+x) over [0,1]. Each partial sum is a polynomial (hence integrable), and |Sn⁢(x)|≤1/(1−|(−x)|) … no, we need a uniform dominator. Since |Sn⁢(x)|=|1−(−x)n+1|/|1+x|≤2/(1+x)≤2 for x∈[0,1], or more simply: each term |(−x)k|≤1, so |Sn⁢(x)|≤n+1 — not a fixed bound. Better: use 1/(1+x) directly as the dominator. We have Sn⁢(x)→1/(1+x) pointwise on [0,1), and |Sn⁢(x)|≤1/(1−x) is not integrable. Actually |(−x)k|=xk≤1, so |Sn⁢(x)|≤(n+1), which is not uniformly bounded. The right approach is different.

Proof.

Step 1: Set up the integral. We have ∫011/(1+x)⁢𝑑x=log⁡(2).

The geometric series gives, for x∈[0,1): 1/(1+x)=∑n=0∞(−1)n⁢xn.

The partial sums are Sn⁢(x)=∑k=0n(−1)k⁢xk. By direct computation:

∫01(−1)k⁢xk⁢𝑑x=(−1)k/(k+1).

So ∫01Sn⁢(x)⁢𝑑x=∑k=0n(−1)k/(k+1).

Step 2: Apply DCT. We need to show ∫01Sn⁢(x)⁢𝑑x→∫011/(1+x)⁢𝑑x.

  • •

    Pointwise convergence: For each x∈[0,1), Sn⁢(x)→1/(1+x) (geometric series).

  • •

    Domination: |Sn⁢(x)|=|1−(−x)n+1|/(1+x)≤(1+xn+1)/(1+x)≤(1+1)/(1+0)=2 for x∈[0,1]. More precisely: |Sn⁢(x)|=|(1−(−x)n+1)/(1+x)|≤2/(1+x)≤2. The constant function 2 is integrable on [0,1].

By the dominated convergence theorem:

∫01Sn⁢(x)⁢𝑑x→∫011/(1+x)⁢𝑑x.

Step 3: Combine.

∑k=0n(−1)k/(k+1)=∫01Sn⁢(x)⁢𝑑x→∫011/(1+x)⁢𝑑x=[log⁡(1+x)]01=log⁡2.

Therefore ∑n=0∞(−1)n/(n+1)=log⁡2. ∎

What connects. This is a model application of the DCT to justify termwise integration of a power series at the boundary of its disk of convergence. The Abel summation theorem gives the same result (if ∑an converges and f⁡(x)=∑an⁢xn, then ∑an=limx→1−f⁡(x)), but the DCT approach is more elementary and directly justifies the interchange of sum and integral. The dominator |Sn|≤2 comes from the closed-form formula for geometric partial sums, which is the key algebraic input. The same technique proves ∫01log⁡(1+x)/x⁢𝑑x=π2/12 and many other series-integral identities.

2. Lean 4 theorem statement

import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.FundThmCalculus
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecificLimits.Normed
import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.InfiniteSum.Basic

open MeasureTheory Set Filter Topology Real

noncomputable section

/-- Main theorem: Σ (-1)ⁿ/(n+1) = log 2. -/
theorem alternating_harmonic_eq_log_two :
    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => (-1 : ℝ) ^ n / (↑n + 1)) (log 2) := by
  sorry

/-- Equivalent tsum formulation. -/
theorem tsum_alternating_harmonic :
    ∑' n : ℕ, (-1 : ℝ) ^ n / (↑n + 1) = log 2 := by
  sorry

/-- ∫₀¹ 1/(1+x) dx = log 2. -/
lemma integral_inv_one_plus :
    ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, 1 / (1 + x) = log 2 := by
  sorry

/-- The partial sum Sₙ(x) = Σₖ₌₀ⁿ (-x)ᵏ = (1-(-x)^{n+1})/(1+x). -/
lemma geom_partial_sum (x : ℝ) (hx : x ≠ -1) (n : ℕ) :
    ∑ k in Finset.range (n + 1), (-x) ^ k =
      (1 - (-x) ^ (n + 1)) / (1 + x) := by
  sorry

/-- ∫₀¹ (-1)ᵏ xᵏ dx = (-1)ᵏ/(k+1). -/
lemma integral_pow_term (k : ℕ) :
    ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * x ^ k =
      (-1) ^ k / (↑k + 1) := by
  sorry

/-- ∫₀¹ Sₙ(x) dx = Σₖ₌₀ⁿ (-1)ᵏ/(k+1). -/
lemma integral_partial_sum (n : ℕ) :
    ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, ∑ k in Finset.range (n + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * x ^ k =
      ∑ k in Finset.range (n + 1), (-1) ^ k / (↑k + 1) := by
  sorry

/-- Domination: |Sₙ(x)| ≤ 2 for x ∈ [0,1]. -/
lemma partial_sum_bound (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) (hx : x ∈ Icc (0:ℝ) 1) :
    |∑ k in Finset.range (n + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * x ^ k| ≤ 2 := by
  sorry

/-- Pointwise convergence: Sₙ(x) → 1/(1+x) for x ∈ [0,1). -/
lemma partial_sum_tendsto (x : ℝ) (hx : x ∈ Ico (0:ℝ) 1) :
    Tendsto (fun n => ∑ k in Finset.range (n + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * x ^ k)
      atTop (𝓝 (1 / (1 + x))) := by
  sorry

/-- DCT application: ∫₀¹ Sₙ → ∫₀¹ 1/(1+x). -/
lemma integral_partial_sum_tendsto :
    Tendsto
      (fun n => ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1,
        ∑ k in Finset.range (n + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * x ^ k)
      atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, 1 / (1 + x))) := by
  sorry

end
